Benham, The Laws of Scientific Hand Reading (1900), Part Second, chapter on the Line of Head. Establishes: straight head line = practical mentality (supported); sloping-to-Luna head line = imagination, departure from purely material thought (supported); writer/poet examples among sloping lines are Benham's illustrative observations, not a monotonic degree rule (explicitly not established); clinical/insanity language is unsafe for this article and not needed.

evidence_basis.canonical_lesson_used_as_proof: No. The canonical lessons/lines/03-head-line.mdx lesson was read only for terminology/navigation consistency (e.g. 'Mount of Luna' naming convention); every interpretive claim in the new article is sourced to the Director evidence note directly, per the task's explicit instruction not to reuse the lesson as proof.

source_preflight.notes: Prevalence/consensus: the claim-risk heuristic's two initial findings ('rarely' describing how head lines run generally, and 'generally' trailing a sentence about mental strength) were both reworded to remove the frequency/consensus framing rather than substituted with a synonym; a manual re-read for the same failure-mode words the heuristic's word list misses in prior tasks ('further', 'consistently', 'typically', 'usual', 'common') found no additional instances. Scientific/historical: every interpretive claim (straight = practical, sloping = imagination, writer/poet examples) is attributed to Benham by name and traced to the evidence note; no claim exceeds what the note authorizes, and no monotonic degree-scaling claim is stated or implied — the article explicitly names and rejects that exact overstatement as a myth. Combination readings: the 'Path in context' section explicitly separates path from length, depth/clarity, and endpoint, links to the relevant companion articles for each, and states plainly that Palmistry Path's approved sources do not set out a specific combined reading for path together with those features, so none is asserted. Vague attribution: no 'modern palmists'/'some writers'/'experts'/unnamed-tradition phrasing; every interpretive claim names Benham specifically. Three drafting-stage references to 'the sources this article draws from' (plural, though only one source is cited) were reworded to 'Benham's reading' for precision. Quotation fidelity: no quotation marks are used anywhere in the article; all Benham content is paraphrased at the level the evidence note supports. Precision/degree extrapolation: the 'Telling the two apart' section explicitly states there is no fixed angle or zone boundary between straight and sloping, and path is framed as a comparative reading only. Observation vs. interpretation: 'Telling the two apart' is pure observation guidance, 'What it's traditionally associated with' is Benham's historical interpretation (explicitly attributed), and 'Path in context'/'Common myths' are Palmistry Path's own editorial framing, kept structurally distinguishable. Safety boundaries: no medical, legal, financial, deterministic-relationship, or predictive-science claim was introduced.
